# Sara Foundation Africa

> A public-benefit organisation headquartered in London, United Kingdom, expanding access to digital education and tech learning, promoting social inclusion and strengthening community capacity for young people, women and underserved communities in Africa.

Sara Foundation Africa reduces barriers to learning and participation through structured digital education, mentoring, practical projects, supportive networks, scholarships and access support, knowledge-sharing, volunteering and community activities. Three learning pathways — CAP (Community Access & Participation Pathway), FLIP (Female Learning & Inclusion Pathway) and EJP (Education Journey Pathway) — translate our charitable purposes into structured routes for learning, inclusion and continued development.

## Charitable focus areas

- Digital Education: structured learning that builds digital literacy, practical skills and confidence to keep learning.
- Social Inclusion: inclusive access to mentoring, supportive networks, resources and development opportunities.
- Community Capacity Building: mentoring, volunteering, peer support and knowledge-sharing.

## Verified impact figures (each measures a different thing; these are not unique individuals)

- 763 CAP learners received fully funded access across Cohorts 1 and 2
- 35+ universities represented across the 8 African countries reached by CAP
- FLIP reaches 6 African countries; together the pathways reach 11 unique countries
- 47 knowledge and expert sessions delivered
- 57 women participated across FLIP fellowship and mentorship activity
- 108 recorded attendances across 3 FLIP workshops
- 100 attendees at CAP Conference 1.0; 93 attendees at FLIP Conference 1.0
- 10 CAP learner projects and 5 FLIP capstone projects
- 2 Talent Showcases and 1 Demo Day
- 170 AI training places delivered with partner organisations
- 705 referrals for placement opportunities across historical activity (referrals are not confirmed placements)
- 1,600 scholarships provided across pathways
- Network of 60+ speakers, trainers, facilitators, mentors and volunteers
- 6,000+ community reach (reach is not the same as learners trained)

Sara Foundation Africa does not guarantee or promise employment through any of its pathways.

## Learning pathways

- [CAP](/programs/cap): Structured digital education, mentoring and practical learning for young people from underserved communities, delivered through CAP Tech Hubs with a Learn, Build, Launch structure and an 80/20 practice-to-learning balance.
- [CAP Apply](/programs/cap/apply): Application form for CAP.
- [FLIP](/programs/flip): Inclusive access to tech learning for women through fellowship, mentorship, workshops and community activity, including a six-week tailored programme.
- [FLIP Apply](/programs/flip/apply): Application form for FLIP.
- [EJP](/programs/gjp): Continued learning through insight sessions, work-readiness education, mentoring, educational exposure and referrals to further learning. Employment is not guaranteed.
- [EJP Express Interest](/programs/gjp/apply): Application form for EJP activity.

## Key facts for citation

- Legal/brand name: Sara Foundation Africa (also "Sara Foundation")
- Headquarters: London, United Kingdom; delivery across 11 African countries
- Founded: 2021
- Mission: Empowering people through tech learning, inclusion and opportunity to build stronger communities
- Pathways: CAP (Community Access & Participation Pathway), FLIP (Female Learning & Inclusion Pathway), EJP (Educational Journey Pathway)
- Website: https://sarafoundationafrica.com
- Contact: info@sarafoundationafrica.com
- Social: https://twitter.com/Sarafoundations, https://www.linkedin.com/company/sara-foundation-africa

## Common questions

**What does Sara Foundation Africa do?** It expands access to digital education and tech learning, promotes social inclusion and strengthens community capacity for young people, women and underserved communities in Africa, through the CAP, FLIP and EJP pathways.

**What do CAP, FLIP and EJP stand for?** CAP is the Community Access & Participation Pathway (delivered via CAP Tech Hubs), FLIP is the Female Learning & Inclusion Pathway (for women), and EJP is the Educational Journey Pathway (continued learning, work-readiness education and referrals).

**Who can join?** Young people and women from underserved communities across Africa, including students, recent graduates and career changers. Applications are made on each pathway's apply page.

**Is CAP free?** CAP and FLIP have a programme fee of £500 / ₦1,000,000. Donations fund scholarships, bursaries and reductions, and partner reference or waiver codes can give fully funded access.

**How long is CAP?** CAP runs as a six-week intensive pathway structured around Learn, Build, Launch, with an 80/20 practice-to-learning balance.

**Does Sara Foundation Africa guarantee jobs?** No. EJP offers work-readiness education, mentoring and referrals; employment is never guaranteed.

**Where is it based?** Headquartered in London, United Kingdom, with programme delivery across 11 African countries and 35+ universities represented.

**How can I support the work?** Donate at /donation, partner at /partnership, or volunteer as a mentor, student ambassador, speaker or trainer at /volunteer.
